chunks: And Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated from Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
O you who believe, the testimony between you, when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest, shall be of two just men from among you, or two others from other than you.

He said: The two from among you are two Muslims, and the two from other than you are from the People of the Book. If you do not find any from the People of the Book, then from the Magians, because among the Magians there is the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the People of the Book regarding the jizyah. That is when a man dies in a foreign land and two Muslims are not found; then two men from the People of the Book are taken as witnesses and are detained after the ʿAṣr prayer.

Then they shall swear by Allah, if you doubt: We shall not sell it for any price, even if he were a near relative, nor shall we conceal the testimony of Allah; indeed, then we would surely be among the sinful.

He said: And that is if the guardian of the deceased doubts their testimony. If it is discovered that they testified falsely, then he has no right to invalidate their testimony until he brings two witnesses who stand in the place of the first two witnesses.
Then they shall swear by Allah: Our testimony is truer than their testimony, and we have not transgressed; indeed, then we would surely be among the wrongdoers.
So when he does that, the testimony of the first two is invalidated, and the testimony of the latter two is accepted. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says:
That is more likely that they will give testimony in its proper manner, or fear that oaths will be returned after their oaths.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ: the People of the Book whose testimony may be used in this case
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: the tax by which a legal status is recognized
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِ: the Magians, mentioned as a fallback category in the absence of Ahl al-Kitāb
key_terms.حِينَ الْوَصِيَّةِ: at the time of making a bequest
key_terms.وَلِيُّ الْمَيِّتِ: the guardian or legal representative of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Who can serve as witnesses to a dying person's bequest if no Muslims are available?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the Qur'anic ruling on testimony for a bequest when death approaches, especially in the circumstance of dying in a foreign land. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام clarifies who may serve as witnesses, how oaths are administered, and how false testimony may be overturned through a second pair of witnesses. The narration is significant for fiqh because it details the legal procedure of testamentary witness testimony and interprets the verses of Sūrat al-Māʾidah in a concrete judicial context.
